texts: In alpha-stat management, blood gases are measured at 37 degrees and kept at a pH of 7.40 without adding carbon dioxide during cooling.
Cerebral blood flow keeps its autoregulation, matched to the brain's metabolism: C is the answer.
pH-stat adds carbon dioxide to keep the pH at 7.40 at the patient's actual temperature; cerebral flow rises, autoregulation is lost and more microemboli reach the brain.
Memory hook: the alpha wolf leaves the gas tanks closed, and the head's own valve keeps the flow steady.
